en: The Moon's gravity is one-sixth of Earth's, so a 60-pound child would weigh only 10 pounds there.
Earth's magnetic north pole is actually a magnetic south pole, which is why the north end of a compass points to it.
A single bolt of lightning heats surrounding air to 30,000 degrees Celsius, making it five times hotter than the sun's surface.
Light travels so fast that it can circle the Earth's equator about seven and a half times in just one second.
Sound travels about fifteen times faster in solid steel than in air, letting you hear a distant train through the tracks first.
Water uniquely expands when it freezes, making solid ice less dense than liquid water so that ice cubes float in your glass.
A hovercraft glides over both land and water by riding on a continuous cushion of air that drastically reduces surface friction.
A pair of tweezers is actually two third-class levers working together, with effort applied between the fulcrum and the load.
Photosynthesis in plant leaves converts radiant energy from sunlight into chemical energy, which is stored as glucose for the plant.
Rubbing your hands together converts kinetic energy into thermal energy through friction, which is why your palms feel warm on a cold day.
An electromagnet is a temporary magnet created when electrical current flows through a coiled wire wrapped around a solid iron core.
Astronauts on the International Space Station experience microgravity not because there is zero gravity, but because they are constantly falling around Earth.
